clicked: read → video Trailers, gameplay clips, time-lapses, cutscenes, talking portraits.

blocks.text: A film is the road only when the creator asks for one; a scene the world can play live is scripted in the world. A film OF THIS WORLD (a trailer, a gameplay clip, a walkthrough) is filmed on a box with a GPU; a scene that is not this world is made with spawn video, or conjured by its path when it runs under 5 seconds or loops. Such a scene plays in a Spawn world you place it in: the one it is for, never a guess; else ask them which. Hand over its file or address only if it is about a Spawn game, this one's story and characters too, whatever use they say. A record button is ui.js code (getDisplayMedia, →game-ui), never a film.

The bar: a clip is a scene the game earns, never a screen it hides behind. A trailer is several shots of real play, each close where its move lands. A cutscene plays once at its cue with the world warm behind it. A backdrop cycles without a seam. A speaking portrait says its one line and hands the screen back.
spawn gpu takes a box and prints ssh gpu: GPU google-chrome, ffmpeg with h264_nvenc, xdotool and Playwright:

ssh gpu 'google-chrome --kiosk "$SPAWN_WORLD_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 20; node play.js & spawn-film 22 take.mp4; spawn-film 22 close.mp4 --camera cam.js' cd /workspace/gpu && ffmpeg -y -i take.mp4 -i close.mp4 -lavfi concat=n=2:a=1 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart trailer.mp4 && spawn upload trailer.mp4

Each take opens the running game in its own browser as a nameless player; your body's page films nothing and draws only for a picture. Your script on the box plays the take's page: a shot brings the player to a thing the game does and plays the move at its target. A test flag or autopilot is not play. A film saves nothing: a flag, key, camera, scene or prop placed for the shoot runs for every player, and the room's players are real: the take's player moves by play alone. A page take of unpublished work goes up with the next publish, so film an update's trailer first.

--camera cam.js flies a camera script (update(ctx, dt) over ctx.self, the camera rig's ctx.self.target your player) over your script's page, with no HUD; it and a prop it ctx.spawns stay on that page. A camera behind your player facing the nearest foe (query) frames the move and its hit; the page's cursor ray and aim axes are its, so the foe sits under a centred mouse and, where the game walks by the aim, forward walks at it. A foe underfoot or underground spins the camera: hold its heading there. spawn-film @v1 @v4 @v9 2 lapse.mp4 --camera cam.js films each version (spawn versions inspect) into one clip, its camera moving on. See each take's frame sheet before the cut: black or loading, wait longer; a camera spinning or inside a thing, film again. The creator hears what the clip shows and its address, for a <video src> in ui.js or a face's material.texture.

The game's page and box play a trailer first, silent and looping (a device set to less motion or less data shows a still with a play button): offer one for the page at hand-over; one asked for the page goes there when done. spawn publish set_trailer --video trailer.mp4 puts it there. See every frame of a clip the creator uploaded; one a stranger should not meet stays off the shelf, the reason said.
A scene made on MiniMax H3

What they hand or name, a photo, clip, dance or game, is the thing itself: look it up first, never memory or old art. spawn video "<what happens>" makes a 5 to 15 second scene with its own sound on MiniMax H3 and prints its address. --image <still> makes a painted or uploaded still its first frame and its shape, --end <still> its last; --seconds the length (5 by default), --aspect a word scene's frame (16x9 by default). --show <name> prints what a clip was made with.
Game code asks one with await ctx.awaitJob(ctx.job("video:generate", { prompt, seconds, aspect })) on the world's fuel.

/cdn/<scene>.mp4 renders the slug's words. /cdn/<still>.png.<action>.mp4 brings a still to life: the still its first frame, the action slug its motion. -saying-<line> in the slug is the spoken line, voiced with the picture. An action ending -loop is seam-cut to cycle, video only; a loop's sound is an sfx-…-loop.mp3 through the engine's audio.

The slug says its length in plain words (-12-seconds, -a-quick-3-second-flash), made to the nearest of 1 to 15 seconds, a loop's at most 9; unnamed, about 6, a loop 2.5 to 6. .aspect-<w>x<h> right before .mp4 is the frame, one of 16x9 9x16 1x1 4x3 3x4 3x2 2x3 21x9 3x1; a slug without it is 16x9, a still its own shape.

<!-- ui.js render() --> <video src="/cdn/value.<sha>.png.gravely-saying-the-crown-is-yours-for-9-seconds.aspect-9x16.mp4" poster="/cdn/value.<sha>.png" playsinline style="width:100%"></video> <video src="/cdn/banner-clouds-drifting-4-second-loop.aspect-3x1.mp4" loop muted autoplay playsinline style="width:100%"></video>

A <scene>.mp4 has no still, so a painted picture is its poster, shown for the minutes a first conjure takes. A cutscene's cue is a data-modal surface fired by a once-only uiEvent (→game-ui), and the rail block game-ui names stays clear under any clip.

A still sings or speaks a sound you have, a line of the creator's vocal or a recorded voice, lips on its time: spawn video --image <still> --audio <sound> makes it on MiniMax H3's lip-sync model and prints its address. The clip runs as long as the sound; a sound under 5 seconds gets silence after it. A song goes a line at a time: cut each line from the vocal in your shell, spawn upload it, make its clip, join them on the song's timing.
